proof_summary: For $p\equiv1\pmod4$, Euler’s criterion rewrites the entries modulo $p$ as $(i^2-m!j)^m$; a binomial/Vandermonde factorization, injectivity of the half-system of squares, and Wilson’s identity $(m!)^2=(-1)^{m+1}$ show that both determinant factors are nonzero. For $p\equiv3\pmod4$, discrete logarithms and Fourier inversion give a matrix factorization whose determinant expansion is paired by a sign-reversing involution on binary Fourier-mode choices: the Fourier coefficients change sign under reflection, while conjugation and row reversal leave the corresponding exponential determinants unchanged, so all terms cancel.
